Generalized estimating equations

Source: R/marginal.R
gee.Rd

Fits a marginal mean model g(E(y)) = X beta with variance phi V(mu) and a working correlation within clusters by the method of Liang and Zeger (1986), with moment estimates of the correlation and scale and a robust (sandwich) covariance. Quasi likelihood models (McCullagh and Nelder 1989, ch. 9) are the independence case: gee(y ~ x, data, family = quasipoisson()) gives the quasi Poisson estimates with a Pearson scale.

Usage

gee(
  formula,
  data,
  id,
  family = stats::gaussian(),
  corstr = c("independence", "exchangeable", "ar1", "unstructured"),
  waves = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  maxit = 50,
  tol = 1e-08
)

Arguments

formula

Mean model formula; may contain an offset.

data

Data frame.

id

Cluster identifier (unquoted column name or vector). Rows of a cluster are taken in data order unless waves is given.

family

A stats family object such as gaussian(), poisson(), binomial(), Gamma(), inverse.gaussian(), quasi(), quasipoisson() or quasibinomial().

corstr

Working correlation: "independence", "exchangeable", "ar1" or "unstructured".

waves

Optional within cluster time index (integers) for "ar1" and "unstructured".

weights

Optional prior weights.

maxit, tol

Iteration limit and convergence tolerance.

Value

An object of class regcomp_gee with coefficients, robust covariance vcov, naive (model based) covariance vcov_naive, alpha (working correlation parameters), scale and fitted.values.

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(g = rep(1:40, each = 4), x = rnorm(160))
d$y <- rpois(160, exp(0.2 + 0.4 * d$x + rnorm(40, 0, 0.4)[d$g]))
gee(y ~ x, data = d, id = g, family = poisson(), corstr = "exchangeable")
#> <regcomp_gee> poisson(log), exchangeable working correlation, 40 clusters
#>              estimate  robust_se        z
#> (Intercept) 0.3373722 0.07980235 4.227597
#> x           0.5769809 0.09642471 5.983745
#>   correlation 0.0899  scale 1.3128
